question: The thick deposits of glacial clay and other materials embedded with moraines in the Kashmir Valley are known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karewa**__.

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karewas** are thick deposits of glacial clay and other materials implanted with moraines. 
 
• The** Kashmir Himalayas** are popular for** Karewa formations, **which are functional for the **cultivation of Zafran, a local variety of saffron.**
 
• Karewas are **marine deposits** in the Valley of Kashmir and **Bhadarwah Valley of the Jammu Division.**
 
• The Karewa origination is a **Plio-Pleistocene glaciofluvial-lacustrine and aeolian loess, according to geographers.**
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce02404f6e3fd07f4253eeac80f7477e3c7726c2681a01e81449ca6e2c4e4b01.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khadir soil **comprises new alluvial soil relatively higher in new silt content from the river, gets replenished with each flooding cycle, and is frequently very fertile.
 
• **Bhangar regions** are beyond the floodplains, which lie more upland, and in contrast to **Khadar, **it comprises **older alluvial soil which is higher in sandy loam content. ​ **
